title: Clinical decision support in dentistry
html: As Wright1 noted in this journal, artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping oral health care across documentation, diagnostics, and patient communication. Within that landscape, AI-powered clinical decision support systems (CDSSs) for detecting caries and periodontal bone loss have rapidly entered clinical practice. These tools hold genuine promise. But a closer look at how they are marketed has revealed a concern the profession has not yet addressed openly: are these systems engineered primarily to support clinical judgment or to influence treatment acceptance?
